## Functions or modules to implement

### Automation surface (§20.E)
- No new script. This extends `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`, which already runs automatically: the review workflow's resolver step calls it (`.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, step `Run Codex resolver, validate, stage, commit`, on a PR push or on an integration sync with conflicts).
- No new supervisor, no database work, and no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.
- The new test is wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which runs on push and pull requests, in the same PR.

### Representative pattern
- For the millisecond clock, follow `_memory_epoch_ms` in `scripts/memory_helpers.sh` (`date +%s%3N`, with a numeric check and a fallback). This script does not source `memory_helpers.sh`, so it gets its own private helper.
- For the tests, follow `tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_retry_state.py`: read the script text with `RESOLVE_SCRIPT`, then extract and run individual functions.

### 1. New script-level state and helpers in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`
Put these right after `_dispatch_integration_judge_now()` (it ends at about line 407) and before the `# EXIT trap — fires the dispatch…` comment. That way they are defined before `trap _resolver_exit_trap EXIT` is installed (about line 430).

A case-insensitive search for `resolver_terminal` over `scripts/` and `tests/` currently finds nothing, so these names do not clash:
- `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_EXIT_CLASS="other"`
- `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_ATTEMPTS=0`
- `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_ATTEMPT_MS=()`
- `_resolver_terminal_attempt_open_ms=""`

Helpers:
- `_resolver_terminal_now_ms`: prints `date +%s%3N` when it matches `^[0-9]+$`. Otherwise it prints `$(( $(date +%s) * 1000 ))`, or `0` if that also fails. It always returns 0.
- `_resolver_terminal_attempt_end`: when `_resolver_terminal_attempt_open_ms` is set, it appends `max(0, now - open)` to `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_ATTEMPT_MS` and clears the open marker. It is idempotent: a second call does nothing.
- `_resolver_terminal_attempt_begin`: calls `_resolver_terminal_attempt_end` first (a safety net for any path that skipped the end call), then sets `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_ATTEMPTS=$((RESOLVER_TERMINAL_ATTEMPTS + 1))` and opens a new timer. Use the assignment form, not `((x++))`, because `((x++))` returns 1 when x is 0 and would trip `set -e`.
- `_resolver_terminal_emit_record <rc>`: always called inside a subshell. It starts with `trap - EXIT; set +e +u`, closes any open attempt, cleans every field (below), and prints exactly one line to stdout:
  `RESOLVER_TERMINAL run_id=<id|none> run_attempt=<n|none> pr=<n|none> attempts=<n> attempt_ms=<n,n,...|none> exit_class=<class> rc=<rc> fp_violations=<n> markers=<n|unknown>`

Field cleaning:
- `run_id`, `run_attempt` and `pr` come from `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` and `PR_NUMBER`. Any value that is not `^[0-9]+$` becomes `none`.
- `attempts` is `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_ATTEMPTS`, or `0` if it is not numeric. It counts attempts actually started, so it stays correct when the no-progress check jumps `attempt` straight to MAX.
- `attempt_ms` keeps only numeric array entries, joined with commas. An empty list prints `none`.
- `exit_class`: when rc is 0 it is `ok`. Otherwise it is `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_EXIT_CLASS` if that is one of `timeout|no_progress|markers|fingerprint|scope|commit|other`, else `other`.
- `rc` is the numeric rc.
- `fp_violations` is `${_fp_count:-}` if numeric, else `0`.
- `markers` is `${_marker_count:-}` if numeric, else `unknown`.

The line never includes a path, branch, URL, model output or token. The helpers make no `gh` calls, write nothing to `GITHUB_ENV`, and read no new environment variables. `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` and `GITHUB_RUN_ID` are set by Actions itself.

### 2. `_resolver_exit_trap` (about lines 420-426)
Insert one line after `local _rc=$?` and before the existing `if`:
`( _resolver_terminal_emit_record "${_rc}" ) 2>/dev/null || true`

Nothing else changes: the `_dispatch_integration_judge_now || true` call on a non-zero rc and `return "${_rc}"` stay exactly as they are. The record comes before the dispatch so it is logged even if the dispatch helper is slow. Running it in a subshell means that a `set -u` or `set -e` failure inside the emitter cannot end the parent trap or change `_rc`.

The trap is still installed only under `if [ -z "${RESOLVER_TEST_REPAIR_RESULT_FILE}" ]`.

### 3. The `--test-repair` branch (about line 1832)
Add one comment line next to the existing `# No integration-judge dispatch…` comment and leave the code alone. The comment explains that no `RESOLVER_TERMINAL` record is emitted here, because the EXIT trap is never installed in `--test-repair` mode (`trap - EXIT` does nothing on this path). Emitting a record would add new behaviour to a path that runs no conflict resolution.

### 4. Per-attempt timing (resolver loop, about lines 3662-4230)
- First line of the loop body, before `emit_conflict_resolver_substate "PreparingWorkspace"`: `_resolver_terminal_attempt_begin || true`.
- `_resolver_terminal_attempt_end || true` immediately before each of the four in-loop `sleep 2` lines (scope-drift retry at about line 3904, attempt-state retry at about 3932, non-zero-exit retry at about 4047, soft-validation retry at about 4229). This keeps the 2-second backoff out of the attempt time.
- On the line right after the loop's unindented closing `done` (the `break` success path): `_resolver_terminal_attempt_end || true`.
- Attempts that end in an `exit` are closed by the emitter inside the trap.
- Do NOT insert anything between `resolver_commit_engine="codex"`, `attempt=1` and the `while` line. `tests/test_review_autofix_claude_fixer_mode.py:1109` and `tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_retry_prelude_render.py:620/976` pin that adjacency and the first unindented `\ndone\n`.

### 5. Exit-class assignments
Each is a single `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_EXIT_CLASS="<tok>"` line placed right before an existing `exit`. The surrounding logic does not change.

| Exit site (about line) | Class |
|---|---|
| 3774 (scope baseline capture fails) | `scope` |
| 3883 (scope cannot be verified) | `scope` |
| 3890 (scope restore cannot be verified) | `scope` |
| 3894 / 3911 (`exit 78`, workspace safety) | `scope` |
| 3900 (exhausted with out-of-scope edits) | `scope` |
| 3921 (attempt state cannot be trusted) | `scope` |
| 3929 (exhausted with out-of-conflict edits) | `scope` |
| 4044 (final attempt exits non-zero) | `timeout` when `_prev_attempt_failure_kind` is `timeout` or `stall_guard`, else `other` |
| 4155, 4168 (both no-progress promotion sites, next to `attempt="${INTEGRATION_SYNC_RESOLVER_MAX_ATTEMPTS}"`) | `no_progress` |
| 4208 (final fingerprint verifier rejects) | `fingerprint`, unless the class is already `no_progress` |
| 4214 (residual markers remain) | `markers`, unless already `no_progress` |
| 4221 (generic exhaustion) | stays `no_progress` if set; else `fingerprint` when `${_fp_count:-0}` > 0; else `other` |
| 4396 (workflow-file / allowlist violation) | `scope` |
| 4423 / 4430 / 4440 (`check_resolver_diff` guard) | `scope` |
| Staging and commit block | `commit` |

The 4044 case is written as an explicit `if`, so the literal `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_EXIT_CLASS="timeout"` appears in the script.

For the staging and commit block: set `commit` once, right after the `check_resolver_diff.sh` success block closes (after about line 4441) and before the first staging command (`git rm -r --cached … node_modules` / `git add`). This covers the staging exits at about lines 4487, 4531 and 4534, and the implicit `set -e` failure of `git commit -m "[ai-merge-resolve] …"`. The `exit 0` paths still record `ok`, because rc 0 overrides the class.

Every other exit after the trap is installed (retry-base restore at 3673, Claude capacity at 3840, `_resolver_fail_closed`, setup failures) keeps the default `other`.

## Data structures affected
- New in-process shell state only: one string, one integer, one integer array and one open-timer marker.
- No files, environment variables, artifacts or GitHub state change.
- One new log line: the `RESOLVER_TERMINAL` stable log prefix.

## API or interface changes
- New contractual log line on stdout, emitted once per resolver run whenever the EXIT trap fires: `RESOLVER_TERMINAL run_id=… run_attempt=… pr=… attempts=… attempt_ms=… exit_class=… rc=… fp_violations=… markers=…`.
- The keys and their order are fixed.
- `exit_class` is one of `ok|timeout|no_progress|markers|fingerprint|scope|commit|other`.
- No change to exit codes, `GITHUB_ENV` outputs, judge dispatch or CLI arguments.

## Decisions

### D1 — Emit inside `_resolver_exit_trap`, in a subshell
- Chosen: `( _resolver_terminal_emit_record "${_rc}" ) 2>/dev/null || true`, placed right after `local _rc=$?` and before the dispatch call.
- Alternatives considered: build the line inline in the trap with `{ …; } || true`; emit after the dispatch.
- Why: under `set -u`, an unbound expansion ends a non-interactive shell even with `|| true`, which could change the exit status from inside the trap. A subshell isolates that failure completely. Emitting before the dispatch makes sure the record lands even if the dispatch helper hangs or fails.

### D2 — Count attempts with a dedicated counter, not `attempt`
- Chosen: `RESOLVER_TERMINAL_ATTEMPTS`, incremented by `_resolver_terminal_attempt_begin`.
- Alternatives considered: read `attempt` from the loop.
- Why: the no-progress check sets `attempt` to MAX, so it would over-report attempts.

### D3 — Time attempts
